0.content:
Chongyun, a young exorcist from a thaumaturge family, is Xingqiu's closest friend and the usual target of his humour. Xingqiu finds him "haunted houses" to practise in, swears he didn't set the traps inside, and cheerfully offers to have a family maid with Sumeru essential-oil training treat the bruises, in exchange for a favour. He also slips Chongyun his carrots and lets him taste Xiangling's riskier dishes. Xingqiu thinks Chongyun is making good progress in martial arts but has not internalised the chivalric code, and needs practice "especially at eating spicy food". Chongyun calls him a prankster to the core and offers to start a "Victims of Xingqiu" alliance, yet admires his chivalry and swordsmanship.

Chongyun is the friend Xingqiu turns to in a real crisis. He asked him to check the house for spirits when his great-grandfather fell ill (5.3, limited event). In the 5.4 Anecdotes Chongyun began transcribing his manuscript and read it aloud with admiration, quoting a poetic chapter header about a heroine called the Flying Fox, until Xingqiu begged him to stop. Xingqiu says Chongyun's handwriting is lovely and that his talismans look better than Xingqiu's prose. In 7.1 (limited event) Xingqiu proposed they be "the Two Heroes of Xingyun".

1.comment: Xingqiu: The Feiyun family: father, brother and Xu
1.content:
Xingqiu's father heads the Feiyun Commerce Guild, one of Liyue Harbor's largest trading houses; its trades include silk and textiles. His elder brother is the heir. Both lecture Xingqiu about skipped studies, his messy room, his handwriting, missed banquets, irregular meals and martial arts. He in turn has developed elaborate ways to avoid them. Once, after a lecture, his brother found the stash of novels under Xingqiu's bed, misunderstood what it was, and ruled that no one would enter Xingqiu's room without permission again. Xingqiu has claimed his brother is "something of a simpleton" whose work he will end up doing. The steward Xu works mainly under Xingqiu, can decipher his letters, and worries when he vanishes from duties such as the silk trade.

The family is a multigenerational household: grandfather and a great-grandfather over a hundred years old live there too. Every Lantern Rite one family member must personally escort supplies to villages outside the harbour. In the 5.4 Anecdotes his brother, who guards his books jealously, handed him the treasured "Chronicle of Cleansing Ink" to improve his calligraphy. It emerged that the brother had long known about the novels and had already ordered a typewriter fitted to Xingqiu's hands. He held it back because he thought Xingqiu's handwriting had real "style and vigor" worth improving, and allowed it for "emergencies". Xingqiu says his brother "never talks about the business with me. He just lets me... live my life."

In his 7.1 birthday letter Xingqiu writes that after weeks of caravans and meetings, his brother privately offered to speak to the family if Xingqiu's heart wasn't in it. Seeing the lines around his brother's eyes and the grey at his temples, Xingqiu could not say no, and resolved to learn from him properly. Canon names neither father nor brother.

2.comment: Xingqiu: Guhua Clan and the Martial Principle
2.content:
The Guhua Clan, once the Guhua Brotherhood, is an old Liyue martial school whose name once "rang like steel throughout the harbor", but which has declined for centuries. Its three secret arts are Light Piercer (polearm), Rain Cutter (sword) and Life Ender (for those who master both). Xingqiu's father enrolled him as a diversion, knowing the clan was nearly dead. Xingqiu revived it: he grasped the ancient "Martial Principle" after four years and wrote a verse on it. In his view, sword and polearm are both arts of the "eye", because a Vision is an extension of the fighter and the weapon an extension of the Vision. The clan head wept and said the clan needed him. The verse is sealed at Wangshan Hall, ostensibly from outsiders, actually because of his handwriting.

His fame started a minor "Guhua renaissance": devotees come looking for the master, and the clan's disciple Sun Yu tells travellers that Xingqiu "wrote a mantra and utterly changed the legacy" of the clan. Bullies still mock the clan's decline. Xingqiu treats his Guhua training as a secret ("our little secret") from his family and from strangers. The clan reveres the wandering hero Guhua as its founder, although it was actually established after his death by Boxuan, who proclaimed himself Guhua's disciple.

3.comment: Xingqiu: A Legend of Sword and the pen name Zhenyu
3.content:
Xingqiu wrote the martial arts novel "A Legend of Sword", based on his own adventures. Liyue publishers rejected it for a setting "as wildly unrealistic as the plot is banal". He printed a few copies himself and slipped them onto Wanwen Bookhouse's shelves; hardly anyone bought one. An Inazuman merchant took a copy home, where it became a permanent bestseller that imitators could not match. Unaware of this, Xingqiu learned of it from the Traveler, who brought him a letter from Yae Publishing House addressed to "Zhenyu". He embarrassedly admitted the pen name and was quietly delighted that people wanted to read him.

He now writes sequels for Yae Publishing House, with Albedo as illustrator. His messy manuscripts need an editor's transcription, so he submits early and sends snacks as thanks. The novelist Gaiman, visiting Liyue, says Zhenyu is huge in Inazuma and Fontaine but unknown at home. Xingqiu tells the Traveler he is writing a novel they may read only once it is "on sale in book stores all over Liyue". According to Chongyun he has also penned a number of short stories.

Some early text named the pen name "Chenqiu"; since 2.2 it is consistently Zhenyu. Venti is an enthusiastic reader of Zhenyu.

4.content:
Xingqiu's 1.0 Story Quest. Looking for the Liyue Teyvat Travel Guide, the Traveler meets Xingqiu at Wanwen Bookhouse; he has spent three years hunting the final volume of Legend of the Shattered Halberd. At Chang the Ninth's home in Qingce Village they find Gentry Maocai's thug Changhu forcing Chang to sell Cor Lapis at 30% of its value. Xingqiu intervenes as a Guhua disciple, is mocked for it, wins the loan of the book, and then fights off the thugs and a Fatui mage. While he sits reading, he sends the Traveler to investigate, and they find that Gentry is supplying the Fatui agent Javert.

Xingqiu then sends a near-illegible letter to the Guild. Xu funds the Traveler to buy up every piece of Cor Lapis in Liyue, paying Chang a fair price. Gentry and Javert try to seize the stock at a Guild warehouse and are beaten; Javert withdraws. Xu arrives and calls Xingqiu "young master", revealing his identity. Xingqiu makes Gentry pay triple the market price and hopes the profit will earn him "a few more days of freedom" from his father. Chang's pawned books return, and he assumes Xingqiu did nothing, until a strange bookmark falls from the returned volume.

5.content: Albedo illustrates Zhenyu's novels for Yae Publishing House under a pen name. Xingqiu plans the illustrations for "each of the major events in the next three volumes" and sends his ideas to "Mr. Kreideprinz". Albedo finds Xingqiu's work interesting and scoffs at Yae Publishing House's attempts to pair him with a better-paying author. The two met in person during the Irodori Festival in Inazuma (2.6, limited event); Albedo noticed something was troubling Xingqiu, and Xingqiu later asked to model for one of his portraits as a reminder of the lesson he had learned.

6.comment: Xingqiu: Handwriting, calligraphy and the typewriter
6.content:
Xingqiu's handwriting is famously dreadful. The Traveler mistook a letter for ancient script or cipher, Hu Tao stumbled reading his riddle aloud, his Guhua verse was locked away, his signature looks like part of the pattern on a box lid, and only one editor at his publisher can read his manuscripts. In the 5.4 Anecdotes he "practised calligraphy" by cutting leaves with his sword in a bamboo grove outside Qingce Village, reading the annotated "Chronicle of Cleansing Ink" by the swordsman-calligrapher Xifan, which his brother, who loves his books as much as his life, had handed him. When that editor fell ill, the Traveler took his dictation. His brother then revealed the custom typewriter.

Words of Gold: at Wanwen Bookhouse he showed the Traveler identical copies of his book priced differently because one signature's last stroke ran wide. He was troubled that a great-grandfather's note or a brother's letter is valued for the name, not the words. The Traveler said they kept every letter he wrote them, and he promised to keep writing in his "finest illegible calligraphy", adding that if his writing ever looks neat, he has either been kidnapped or really wants to see them.

7.content: Hu Tao, director of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, is one of his circle. He refuses to judge her by rumours and says you must find out what someone is really after. She wants to feed him material for a ghost story and once had to read his handwriting aloud. Xiangling is a friend whose new dishes he avoids. He advises watching her face when she returns with ingredients, and usually passes her tasting tests to Chongyun. Xingqiu, Chongyun, Hu Tao and Xiangling turn up together at festivals (limited events). In 6.3 they puzzled over a photo of a moon apparently "eaten" by Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer; the Traveler explained lunar eclipses, though the image did not match a normal one, and the four went to watch for the anomaly themselves.

8.content: Yun Jin is a Liyue opera singer and playwright. Xingqiu sometimes spends "a moment of solitude" sampling her latest drink at Heyu Tea House, and keeps a jar of tea leaves under his bed for the day her inspiration dries up, so the heroic plays keep coming. She warns that he is clever, sharp-witted and quick to make anyone who drops their guard the butt of a joke.

9.content: The bookstall on Feiyun Slope in Liyue Harbor is the place Xingqiu says he would miss most if it disappeared, with the Guhua Clan somewhere in the top ten. He tracks its delivery schedule (once questioning Gaming about it), proposes detours there mid-adventure, and secretly shelved copies of his own novel there. It is where he met the Traveler.

10.content: In limited-time Lantern Rite events: in 2.4 he escorted the Guild's festival supplies to Qingce Village because his brother had done it the previous year. When Treasure Hoarders attacked, the escort routed them and captured one; he declined Keqing's offered reward, and stayed with Chongyun to guard the village. In 3.4, after Xinyan and Hu Tao's concert, he dined with friends at Xinyue Kiosk, met Zhongli and Xiao, was caught tossing his carrots into Chongyun's bowl, and was startled to hear that Guoba, whom Xiangling had told him was once the Stove God, would make picky eaters finish their carrots. Venti arrived and nearly exposed the Zhenyu name; Xingqiu told Chongyun Venti was a family business partner, and when Hu Tao and Xiangling pressed him, "confessed" that he was a fan of Venti's poetry, with Chongyun backing the story. Earlier, in 2.1 (Moonlight Merriment), he fetched Keqing a book on the Stove God.

11.comment: Xingqiu: The great-grandfather and the fetor (Springtime Charms)
11.content: During the limited-time 5.3 Lantern Rite event, Xingqiu's great-grandfather, over a hundred years old, collapsed into a coma after visiting Qingce Village. Doctors could not diagnose it, and the butler insisted it was a curse. Xingqiu brought Chongyun, who sensed a deathly chill but no spirit, then went to Baizhu, who found the same illness in Timaeus. Xingqiu suspected the god Tao Dou, whom he had read about in a dubious street-vendor book. His brother contacted the funeral parlor and his father and grandfather fasted and prayed. The cause was a surge of fetor, which Hu Tao and the Traveler stopped with a risky ceremony; his great-grandfather recovered. Xingqiu promised the Traveler that they would always find a helping hand at the Feiyun Commerce Guild. He admitted he had never been as close to the old man as his father and grandfather, since by Xingqiu's childhood he was already speaking little.

12.content: In the limited-time 2.6 event, Yae Publishing House invited Xingqiu to Inazuma's Irodori Festival. He talked his father into it by citing the promotion of Theater Mechanicus, and was thrilled to meet his illustrator Albedo. Learning that the festival plan required him to sign stacks of books, he arrived early to practise, without success. The Traveler (after meeting Kazuha) suggested using seals for consistent signatures, and the authors agreed. He travelled with Liyue's delegation of calligraphers, painters and players, with the steward Xu.

13.content: At the limited-time 4.1 Neighboring Nations Congenial Poetry Gala at the Stone Gate, hosted by Hu Tao and Venti, Xingqiu won the first-day riddle contest. His prize, reluctantly accepted, was a buy-one-get-one coupon for Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's high-end customised service. He then joined an investigation into a mysterious transparent entity Chongyun had spotted, pairing with Mika and Noelle, and was puzzled afterwards when Chongyun flatly refused another haunted-house outing.

14.comment: Xingqiu: The nameless heroine and folklore research
14.content: The Traveler treats Xingqiu as a living reference library. In 2.4 (Interlude Chapter) he warned them not to bid on the one piece of Sunset Vermillionite the Guild was auctioning on someone's behalf, since he expected it to go for over 500 million Mora, and pointed them to the rumoured abode of the adeptus Sea Gazer. In Xianyun's Story Quest (4.4) he recounted the chivalric-novel "nameless heroine" who fought bandits and evil spirits during a terrible drought fifty years ago, fell in love with an exorcist of Mt. Tianheng, and vanished into the mountains. He marked three places she appears in the novels (Wangshu Inn, north of Jueyun Karst and Qingyun Peak), reflecting that the magic of such novels is glimpsing a noble soul in a few paragraphs.

key: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon
15.comment: Xingqiu: Moonchase 7.1 and the Wind Reader
15.content: In the limited-time 7.1 Moonchase Festival event, Xingqiu, Chongyun and Hu Tao helped Gaming protect a fragile cargo from spirit-possessed monsters in Dihua Marsh. Xingqiu let Chongyun do most of the fighting "as a golden opportunity" for him. He met the soul-fragment of Lan Junming, the Wind Reader of the Eight Adepts, telling him that Liyue has no "Tianheng Sect" and that the Guhua Clan taught him Raincutter. At the moon-viewing at Wangshu Inn, when Hu Tao proposed "New Eight" titles, he suggested he and Chongyun be "the Two Heroes of Xingyun". Afterwards he asked the Millelith for a copy of their report so his brother might forgive him for skipping lessons: he avoided studying to help, not the reverse.

16.content: Beidou calls him "kid" and ruffles his hair. Ningguang gets a careful "no comment". Yelan, who deals with his family, seems kind and mature at the family home and completely different elsewhere, and predicts he will outsmart everyone around him. Shenhe looks at him fiercely, perhaps because of what he does to her nephew Chongyun. Yanfei, whose meetings with the Guild are attended by the head of the house, found the youngest son eloquent, well-mannered and able to follow her reasoning: "definitely not a simpleton". Ganyu notes he doesn't care for the textile business, presumably because he has more important things to do. Gaming's agency carries Guild goods; Xingqiu admires him as a real-life wuxia hero. Zhongli was entertained by his father and brother as a high-profile guest, which made Xingqiu want to investigate him. Qiqi intrigues him. Xinyan's performances disturb his reading.
